---
title: "Calculate traits from images"
author: "Patrick Pata"
date: "2025-11-26"
output: html_document
---

This script is for calculating trait values from the segmented copepod images.

This file replaces parts of a few deprecated files including UPV6_lipidscape_analysis.Rmd and lipid and biomass concentrations UVP.Rmd.

1. Calculate carbon content from segmented images
2. Apply random forest model to estimate carbon content from non-segmented images
3. Organize the trait values
4. Calculate the diapause respiration rate and duration relative to the in situ temperature of where the image was captured
5. Export data
6. Plot the results with the LOKI sizes and literature values


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# 0. Load libraries and data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(cowplot)
library(ggtext)

# The segmented images and morphological traits of calanoids
load("data/uvp6_CNN_segmentations_morphotraits_20251208.RData")

# The CTD data temperature and region names/color
load("data/ctd_temperature_100m_averages.RData")

# The random forest model
load("functions/random_forest_carbon_trait_models.RData")

theme_set(theme_bw() +
            theme(text = element_text(size=14)))
source("functions/lipid_pump_toolkit.R")

```


#  1. Convert pixels to traits for segmented images
## Derive volume, dry weight, and carbon
```{r}
uvpRes <- 0.073
# Conversion factor to get total lipid mg C from total lipid mg used in Schmidt et al. 2018 based on 36-carbon chain lengths in (Kattner & Graeve 1991) 
lambda <- (36*12) / (36*12 + 2*36 + 2*16)
# Conversion factor to get prosome biomass (mg C) from biovolume (mm3)
vol2massC <- mean(c(0.14373,0.1177,0.1902)) # average of 3 Calanus species in (McConville et al. (2016)

# Conversion factor from mm3 -> WW -> C
# If density asssumed as 1, the value below is the Carbon % Wet weight
# 0.09 is the average for all calanoid copepod species
# 0.0766 is the average for calanoid copepod species except lipid sac forming species
prosomeWW2C <- 0.09# 0.07666


# *** For the CNN segmented images ***
segmented.images <- segmented.images %>% 
  
# Calculate traits from pixels
  mutate(lipid_area_mm2 = lipid_pixels * uvpRes * uvpRes,
         prosome_area_mm2 = prosome_pixels * uvpRes * uvpRes,
         prosome_length_mm = prosome_major * uvpRes) %>% 
  # Calculate minor axis based on prosome/lipid area and major axis (in pixels)
  mutate(minor_derived = (prosome_pixels / (pi * prosome_major/2)) * 2) %>% 
    # Calculate biovolume of prosome approximated as spheroid
  mutate(prosome_biovolume_mm3 = 4/3 * pi * 
           (prosome_major/2 * uvpRes) * ((minor_derived/2 * uvpRes)^2)) %>% 
  
  # Calculate lipid sac volume based on Tarling et al. (2022) eq1 derived from Miller et al. (1998) note that this is  based on cyclindrical volume approximation. According to Miller et al. (1998) the oblate spheroid volume approximation is less accurate
  mutate(lipid_volume_mm3 = 
           (pi * lipid_area_mm2 ^ 2)/(4 * lipid_major * uvpRes)) %>% 
  
# (Calculate lipid carbon based on area following Vogedes et al. 2010 with coefficients for 3 Arctic Calanus species
  mutate(totallipid_mass_mg = 0.197 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.38)) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mg = 0.167 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.42)) %>%  
  
  # Calculate lipid carbon mass
  mutate(lipid_mass_mgC = totallipid_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mgC = waxester_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  
   # Calculate the carbon content of the prosome excluding the lipid sac
  mutate(structural_carbon_mgC = (prosome_biovolume_mm3 - lipid_volume_mm3) * 
           prosomeWW2C) %>% 
  
  mutate(prosome_total_mgC = structural_carbon_mgC + waxester_mass_mgC) %>% 
  
  # Calculate lipid fullness as % carbon in lipid sac WE
  mutate(lipid_fullness = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_total_mgC * 100)

```

# 2. RF for unsegmented images
```{r}
other.calanoid.images <- all.copepods.uvp6 %>% 
  filter(object_id %notin% segmented.images$object_id) %>% 
  # only include > 3 mm
  filter(major_length_mm >= 3) %>% 
  filter(traits_from_RF == T) %>% 
  # only include validated
  filter(object_annotation_status == "validated")

# Apply the Random forest models which already predict for structural and lipidWE carbon in mgC
other.calanoid.images$structural_carbon_mgC <- 
  predict(rf.model.prosome,
          newdata = other.calanoid.images %>% 
            select(Major:PerimMajor))

other.calanoid.images$waxester_mass_mgC <- 
  predict(rf.model.lipid,
          newdata = other.calanoid.images %>% 
            select(Major:PerimMajor))

# Calculate total carbon and lipid fullness

other.calanoid.images <- other.calanoid.images %>% 
  mutate(prosome_total_mgC = structural_carbon_mgC + waxester_mass_mgC) %>% 
  mutate(lipid_fullness = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_total_mgC * 100) %>% 
  mutate(source = if_else(object_annotation_category == "Calanoida",
                          "RF Calanoida", NA),
         source = if_else(object_annotation_category == "Copepoda<Maxillopoda",
                          "RF Copepoda", source),
         source = if_else(object_annotation_category %in% 
                            c("Calanus","top-bottom<with visible lipid sac",
                              "side<with visible lipid sac"),
                          "RF Calanus spp", source))
```


# 3. Organize data
```{r}
indiv_traits <- segmented.images %>% 
  select(object_id, object_annotation_category, source,
         Site = sample_stationid, Cruise = sample_cruise,
         sample_id, object_depth_max,
         Major, prosome_length_mm,
         prosome_total_mgC, structural_carbon_mgC,
         waxester_mass_mgC, lipid_fullness) %>% 
  bind_rows(other.calanoid.images %>% 
              select(object_id, object_annotation_category, source,
                     Site = sample_stationid, Cruise = sample_cruise,
                     sample_id, object_depth_max,
                     Major, 
                     prosome_total_mgC, structural_carbon_mgC,
                     waxester_mass_mgC, lipid_fullness)) %>% 
  
  # Add the ctd temperature data for the depth where individual was captured
  # Assign the ctd file name for the profiles
  left_join(uvp6_ctd_match %>% 
              distinct(Site, Cruise,
                       ctd_filename, profile_group, region),
            by = join_by(Site, Cruise)) %>% 
  
  # Exclude the images from Ungava bay since no CTD data and lone region for analysis
  filter(region != "Ungava Bay") %>% 
  
  # Assign 100 m depth bin
  mutate(temp_depth_bin = floor(object_depth_max/100)*100) 
  
# Join the temperature data based on the filename and temp_depth_bin

# Could return NA temperature when the image depth is a bit lower than the max CTD data (e.g. 701m image when CTD goes until 600-700m bin) ... for now use the regional average

temp_data_A <- indiv_traits %>% 
  left_join(temp_profiles_100m %>% 
              select(ctd_filename = filename,
                     temp_depth_bin = depth_bin,
                     temperature_degC = temp.mean),
            by = join_by(ctd_filename, temp_depth_bin)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(temperature_degC))

# profiles with no matching temperature data, use the regional averages for the depth layer
temp_data_B <- indiv_traits %>% 
  filter(object_id %notin% temp_data_A$object_id) %>% 
  left_join(region_temp_profiles_100m %>% 
              select(region,
                     temp_depth_bin = depth_bin,
                     temperature_degC = reg.temp.mean),
            by = join_by(region, temp_depth_bin))

# Merge the temperature data and join with the indiv_traits dataframe
indiv_traits <- indiv_traits %>% 
  left_join(bind_rows(temp_data_A, temp_data_B) %>% 
              select(object_id, temperature_degC),
            by = join_by(object_id)) %>% 
  mutate(temperature_kelvin = temperature_degC + 273.15) %>% 
  select(-temperature_degC)

# TODO Note, change the depth bin to deeper for individuals at surface since may be too cold?
rm(temp_data_A, temp_data_B)
```


# 4.Calculate diapause respiration rate, potential diapause duration, and total C respired
```{r}
# Adjust respiration rate based on temperature
indiv_traits <- indiv_traits %>% 
  
  # Calculate diapause respiration rate and duration
  mutate(mass_ugC = structural_carbon_mgC * 1000,
         WE_ugC = waxester_mass_mgC * 1000) %>% 
  mutate(respirationRate_ugCday = 
           (2.3*10^-7) * (mass_ugC^0.75) * 
           exp(0.6 * (temperature_kelvin-273)/ 
                 ((8.62*10^-5)*temperature_kelvin*273)) 
         * 86400) %>% 
  mutate(diapauseDuration_day = 
           (0.8*WE_ugC)/(respirationRate_ugCday)) %>% 

# At individual level, calculate the amount of carbon respired by each individual. Then calculate the abundance represented by each individual in every 5 m bin, then calculate the carbon respired and mortality of the 5m-bin fraction of the assemblage.

  # Cap the diapause duration capped to 240 days
  mutate(diapauseDuration_day_cap = if_else(diapauseDuration_day > 240,
                                                240, diapauseDuration_day)) %>% 
  # The total C respired for the entire duration of diapause by the individual (ug C)
  mutate(diapause_resp_by_indiv_ugC = 
           respirationRate_ugCday * diapauseDuration_day_cap) %>%  
  # mutate(percent_WE_respired = diapause_resp_by_indiv_ugC/WE_ugC * 100) %>% 
  select(-c(mass_ugC, WE_ugC, diapauseDuration_day_cap)) 


# Curate columns
indiv_traits <- indiv_traits %>% 
  left_join(region_rename, by = "region") %>% 
  select(-c(ctd_filename)) %>% 

# Clarify sources
  # Assign source details, for non-"Calanus" category, identify categ and size class
  mutate(source = if_else(source == "CNN_segmentation", 
                          "CNN segmentation", source),
         source = if_else(source == "manual_segmentation",
                          "Manual segmentation", source)) %>% 
  mutate(source = factor(source,
                          levels = c("CNN segmentation", "Manual segmentation",
                                     "RF Calanus spp",
                                     "RF Calanoida", "RF Copepoda")))

```

# 5. Export trait data
The indiv_traits dataframe includes images of individuals classified as "Calanus spp" and were segmented manually or with CNN (or the RF predictions when the CNN was bad). It also includes the RF predicted structural and lipid carbon values for images with major axis length >3 mm and were validated and classified as Calanoida/Copepoda, which are likely to be Calanus spp.
```{r, eval=FALSE}
save(indiv_traits, 
     file = "data/uvp6_images_calculated_traits_20251208.RData")
```

## Get LOKI trait values
